description:
You are a metallurgist analyzing a sample of hot-rolled carbon steel to determine its mechanical properties. Your task is to quantify the percentage of the **Pearlite phase** (dark/textured regions) versus the Ferrite phase (light regions) in the provided microstructure image.

Image Location: `~/Fiji_Data/raw/metallurgy/steel_microstructure.jpg`

**Standard Operating Procedure (SOP):**
1. Open the image and convert it to **8-bit grayscale** (`Image > Type > 8-bit`).
2. Apply a **Median Filter** with a radius of **2.0 pixels** to reduce noise (`Process > Filters > Median...`).
3. Segment the Pearlite phase using **Auto Threshold** with the **'Otsu'** method (`Image > Adjust > Auto Threshold`). Ensure you are selecting the **dark** regions (Pearlite) as the foreground.
4. Measure the **Area Fraction** (%) of the Pearlite phase.
   - Ensure `Analyze > Set Measurements` includes 'Area Fraction'.

**Required Outputs:**
1. Save the binary segmentation mask as `~/Fiji_Data/results/metallurgy/pearlite_mask.png`.
2. Save the measurement results table as `~/Fiji_Data/results/metallurgy/phase_measurements.csv`.
3. Create a text report at `~/Fiji_Data/results/metallurgy/report.txt` containing exactly one line with the format: `Pearlite_Fraction: XX.X` (where XX.X is your measured percentage).

Your result will be compared against a ground truth value calculated using the same standard algorithms.
